subject: Efficient Scripting: Multiple Constraints in a SEM

messages.author: fe3f62b5f6c69699
messages.subject: Efficient Scripting: Multiple Constraints in a SEM
parts:
Hello everyone

Does anyone know how to fix the covariances of more than two exogenous variables in a SEM at zero in one line (without the "orthogonal" argument)?

My extensive script with constraints over multiple lines is (simplified):

model <- '
PERT   =~ pdt1 + pdt2 + pdt3                  # PERT is a "pure" enogenous latent variable
UB       =~ ubp1 + ubp2 + ubt1 + ubt2     # UB is endogenous and exogenous
           
GST    =~ gstp1 + gstp2 + gstp3             # GST, SaC are exogenous latent variables
SaC     =~ sacp1 + sacp2 + sacp3
           
PERT  ~ UB + GST                                 # PERT is regressed on UB, GST
UB       ~ SaC                                          # UB is regressed on SaC
           
GST  ~~ 0*UB                                       # GST and UB are uncorrelated
GST  ~~ 0*SaC                                     # GST and SaC are uncorrelated
 '
After having tried out, I guess the two blue lines can be integrated in one line:

      GST ~~ 0*UB + 0*SaC

Even though this seems to work fine (same results as the extensive script), the plus sign "+" irritates me because covariances are not "added up". Therefore I would like to check if anyone can verify my guess.

Any feedback is much appreciated!

Best whishes
Boris

PS: I cannot use the "orthogonal" argument, because in other, more comprehensive models some of the exogenous variables need to correlate.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Efficient Scripting: Multiple Constraints in a SEM
parts: Does anyone know how to fix the covariances of more than two exogenous variables in a SEM at zero in one line (without the "orthogonal" argument)?

It doesn't need to be on one line, if that's easier.  Syntax can be a character vector of length > 1, so you can use paste() to assemble different script components pretty automatically with variable names.  An adaptation from the ?cfa help page:

HS.model <- c(paste0("visual =~ x", 1:3), paste0("textual =~ x", 4:6), paste0("speed =~ x", 7:9))
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit)

The same principle works for specifying a set of orthogonalities.  You could even do so for an entire (sub)matrix using outer() with paste():

varnames <- paste0("x", 1:6)
covstruc <- outer(varnames, varnames, function(x, y) paste(x, "~~", y))
satMod <- c(paste(varnames, "~ 1"), # mean structure
            covstruc[lower.tri(covstruc, diag = TRUE)]) # cov structure
cat(satMod, sep = "\n")
